title: Codegen defects 1–11: generate the correct code, or refuse to compile?
why: Defects 1, 2, 3 and 8 to 11 compile today and store wrong values with no message. Two examples: MOVE prints 123 as $1.23, and SET X = NUM*2 + (NUM*3+1) gives 31 instead of 26. Your 14 September rule says that what compiled in 1962 must compile here.
built: Handle prototypes are approved by both reviewers, with CI green: draft PRs #167 (defects 1–2), #168 (8–11) and #169 (3–4). Interactive records with real runs for each option: defects 1–2 and defects 8–11.

opts.t: Handle them: generate the correct code wherever the manuals show the code
opts.d: Merge #167, #168 and #169 one at a time, each with one more review round. Defect 10 keeps the 1962 behaviour, as you ruled on 25 October.

opts.t: Refuse them: each shape gets a named message
opts.d: Close the three drafts. About ten shapes the manuals show stop compiling, including the 1962 manual's own SET K=K+2.

title: Defect 6, reopening files after CLOSE ALL FILES: what severity, and how far should the check look?
why: J forbids it, and D6.3 says to diagnose it. Today the compiler says nothing, and the run silently overwrites the tape.
built: Prototype: draft #170, approved by both reviewers. The record shows the listing line and the run for each severity.

opts.t: Severity 4, keep the OPEN, detect the straight case only
opts.d: Catches a CLOSE ALL FILES followed later by an OPEN ALL FILES, with no label or jump between them. Under the run gate the job compiles but does not run.
opts.pre: 948,00  4  -OPEN ALL FILES- FOLLOWS -CLOSE ALL FILES-. FILES CLOSED BY THAT FORM MAY NOT BE REOPENED. (NON-HISTORICAL.)

opts.t: Severity 3, delete the OPEN, straight case only
opts.d: The job does not run, and the deleted OPEN changes the object deck.

opts.t: Severity 1, a note only
opts.d: The job runs and loses the second tape's data in silence.

opts.t: Severity 4, flag any OPEN later in the text
opts.d: Wider, but it also flags some correct programs.

recwhy: Severity 4 with the OPEN kept reports the error and leaves the generated code as written. The straight case is the only one the compiler can prove without a flow graph.

opts.t: The listing
opts.d: Our compiler keeps refusing the object deck at those sites. Only the refusal labels change.

opts.t: The object deck
opts.d: We would invent code for every site the 1962 compiler flagged: 26 undefined names, GET and FILE with no file, and an empty GRAND.

title: A column 72 continuation with no card after it: what message?
why: On the last card of a Data or Environment group, a punched column 72 asks for a continuation card that never comes. The compiler accepts this in silence. The manuals do not cover the error, so HANDOVER left the message to you.
built: Prototype: draft #177, reviewed. It prints the message only under --pedantic, as D0.8 requires. Default output and the goldens are unchanged.

opts.t: New message 949,00, class 1, --pedantic only
opts.d: The entry keeps every punched card. The note is the same kind as 919 and 920.
opts.pre: 2,00  1  COLUMN 72 PUNCHED, BUT NO CONTINUATION CARD FOLLOWS. ENTRY ASSUMED COMPLETE. (NON-HISTORICAL.)

opts.t: Reuse the Procedure division's message 62,00
opts.d: It says a period was assumed, but no period is added. J 02.06.02 forbids a period there.
opts.pre: 2,00  1  PREVIOUS CARD NOT PROPERLY TERMINATED. PERIOD ASSUMED.

opts.t: No message: keep accepting it in silence
opts.d: Close #177 and remove the parked item.

recwhy: Message 62's text would be false at this site. A note under --pedantic changes nothing about the 1962 behaviour.

title: W2, the sources page: which copy rules apply to the generated pages?
why: Two of your 10 August rules were written for prose written for the site. Rule E3 marks a manual typo [sic]. Rule D5 bans the em dash. W2 prints whole transcriptions and the whole language reference, which holds about 630 em dashes. web-copy.md section 6 now lists both questions.
built: Built on branch w2-sources: 358 generated pages, every link and anchor checked by a test, and served and fetched locally. It currently follows the recommended option.

opts.t: Apply both rules only to text written for the site
opts.d: Whole transcriptions show the page exactly as the conversions do, with no [sic]. The reference keeps its dashes.

opts.t: Mark every typo and strip the dashes from the reference
opts.d: Needs a typo list, and a mark that copying leaves out. Edits about 630 dashes in the definition.

opts.t: Leave the reference off the site for now
opts.d: Link to GitHub instead. The scans and transcriptions still ship.

why: M7 compares our reconstruction with the surviving 1963 processor, and that comparison is the project's headline result. Once the seal is open, every later decision is contaminated. Nothing is built for this call: under D0.9, even listing the archive counts as reading it.

opts.t: After the open calls above are settled and merged
opts.d: Settle defects 1–11, defect 6 and the M6-9 question, then unseal. Every reconstruction call is then fixed before anyone looks.

title: A BEGIN SECTION with no name: diagnose it, and with which message?
why: F p. 26 says a section starts with its name and a period, then BEGIN SECTION. Today S1. BEGIN SECTION, BEGIN SECTION. opens two sections, both named S1, and one END S1 leaves the second one open (only message 66 fires, at the end of the program). An unnamed BEGIN SECTION. followed by a bare END. draws nothing. No 1962 message covers this.
built: Probed on master today; the cause is procedure_parser.dart:1200, which gives every BEGIN clause the sentence's one label. Not built: the message is your call.

opts.t: Delete the sentence with message 196, as M2-12 does for other illegal clause mixes
opts.d: Attested message, same precedent as M2-12. The section never opens, so later ENDs may draw 65.

opts.t: Message 192, as D1.5 uses for a misplaced key word
opts.d: Attested message; the clause is dropped and the sentence kept.

opts.t: A new non-historical message (D9.12)
opts.d: Exact wording, but no 1962 source.

opts.t: Leave it: the 1962 compiler may have accepted it
opts.d: Under your 14 September rule, a shape it compiled must compile. No evidence either way.

recwhy: 196 is a real 1962 message, and M2-12 already uses it for clauses that may not share a sentence. That keeps us inside attested behaviour.
